Questions: How do I decide which field to choose: AI, Data Science, Cybersecurity, or Web Development?
Answers: Start by exploring what interests you most. AI focuses on intelligent systems, Data Science on analyzing data, Cybersecurity on protecting systems, and Web Development on building websites and applications. Try a small project in each field, explore entry-level job requirements, and choose based on your interest, strengths, and willingness to learn.

Questions: What career opportunities are available for computer science graduates in Pakistan and abroad?
Answers: CS graduates can explore software development, web and mobile development, AI, data analytics, cybersecurity, cloud computing, QA engineering, and DevOps. Opportunities vary by location and experience, so research current job postings and required skills in your target market before choosing a path

Questions: Which industry skills should I learn beyond my university syllabus?
Answers: Focus on practical programming, Git and GitHub, databases, problem-solving, debugging, teamwork, communication, and technical documentation. Depending on your target role, you may also need frameworks, cloud platforms, testing tools, or deployment skills.

Questions: How can I determine whether I am ready to apply for an internship?
Answers: You do not need to know everything before applying. You should understand programming fundamentals, be able to explain at least one project, use Git at a basic level, and show that you can learn independently. Compare your skills with internship descriptions and apply when you meet a reasonable portion of the requirements.

Questions: How important are CGPA, projects, and certifications when applying for jobs?
Answers: Their importance depends on the employer and role. Some employers use CGPA as an initial filter, while projects demonstrate practical ability and certifications can validate specific skills. Prioritize strong fundamentals and relevant projects, and maintain a reasonable CGPA rather than relying on only one achievement

Questions: Should I start my career at a startup or an established company?
Answers: A startup may offer broader responsibilities and faster exposure to different tasks, but its processes and mentorship may be less structured. An established company may provide formal training, defined roles, and established workflows. Compare the learning opportunities, manager support, work culture, compensation, and stability of the specific opportunity.

Questions: How can I identify the gaps between my current skills and industry requirements?
Answers: Choose a target job role and review several recent job descriptions. Make a list of recurring technical and soft skills, then compare them with your current abilities and projects. Prioritize the most frequently required skills and build evidence of those skills through projects, practice, or internships.

Questions: Should I specialize in one field or learn multiple technologies?
Answers: Build a strong foundation in programming, data structures, databases, and software development practices first. Then develop deeper skills in one area while learning enough related technologies to work effectively. You can broaden your expertise as your career goals become clearer.

Questions: How can I get my first internship when I have no professional experience?
Answers: Build two or three projects that demonstrate practical skills, organize your code on GitHub, and prepare a focused one-page CV. Apply to internships, university opportunities, and entry-level programs. Highlight coursework, projects, teamwork, and relevant technical skills instead of claiming experience you do not have.

Questions: How should I prepare for a technical interview as a computer science student?
Answers: Revise programming fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, databases, object-oriented programming, and basic operating-system or networking concepts relevant to the role. Practice solving problems while explaining your reasoning. Prepare to discuss the design, challenges, and technical decisions behind your own projects

Questions: How can I find internship opportunities that are not publicly advertised?
Answers: Connect with alumni, faculty members, university career offices, and professionals working in your target field. Attend career events and technical meetups, and send concise messages explaining your interests and relevant skills. Ask whether their teams expect to offer internships rather than immediately requesting a job.

Questions: What questions should I ask an alumnus during a mentorship session?
Answers: Ask about their transition from university to work, the skills they use most, how they found their first opportunity, and what they would do differently as a student. You can also ask about portfolio expectations, workplace challenges, and learning resources. Prepare questions based on their actual career experience.

Questions: What mistakes do fresh computer science graduates commonly make?
Answers: Common mistakes include relying only on grades, neglecting practical projects, copying code without understanding it, ignoring communication skills, and applying without tailoring a CV. Another mistake is chasing every new technology instead of developing strong fundamentals. Focus on consistent practice and demonstrable skills

Questions: How can I maintain a professional relationship with an alumnus after mentorship
Answers: Send a brief thank-you message, mention a useful takeaway, and follow through on any advice you received. Share a relevant progress update occasionally without expecting an immediate response. Maintain the relationship through genuine professional interaction rather than contacting them only when you need a referral.

Questions: How can I ask an alumnus for a job referral without sounding demanding?
Answers: First, build context by learning about the alumnus's work and explaining your relevant experience. If a suitable role exists, ask politely whether they would feel comfortable referring you. Share your CV and the job link, and make it clear that you understand if they are unable to help.

Questions: Is it useful to connect with alumni who work in a field different from mine?
Answers: Yes. Professionals in other fields can help you understand transferable skills, alternative career paths, and how different teams collaborate. Their experiences may also help you discover interests you had not previously considered. However, seek role-specific advice from people with relevant experience when making technical career decisions

Questions: Can academic assignments be included in my professional portfolio?
Answers: Yes, if they demonstrate relevant skills and you are permitted to share them. Choose assignments that show meaningful problem-solving, improve their documentation, and explain what you learned. Avoid uploading confidential course material or presenting copied code as your own work.

Questions: How can I switch to another computer science field after already learning a different one?
Answers: Identify which of your current skills transfer to the new field, then list the additional skills required for entry-level roles. Build a small project that demonstrates the new skills, revise your CV to emphasize relevant experience, and connect with professionals in that area. You can transition gradually rather than abandoning everything you have already learned

Questions: What is the minimum attendance required to sit in a final examination?
Answers: At least 75% attendance in each course is required to be eligible for that course’s terminal examination.
